results.name: Half Neck Rolls
instructions: Stand upright with your feet shoulder width apart and cross your arms over your chest.
Lower your chin toward your chest and slowly roll your head from the left side toward the right side.
Reverse the movement and roll your head back toward the left, keeping your chin moving across the front of your chest.
Continue moving slowly from side to side for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Keep your shoulders relaxed and away from your ears.
Do not roll your head backward or drop it behind your shoulders.
Stop if you feel pain, dizziness, or tingling.
Inhale as you reach one side and exhale as your chin moves across your chest.
results.description: Half Neck Rolls is a beginner single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the levator scapulae (neck). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the flexibility category. Secondary muscles: Upper Back.

results.name: Hamstring Lying Curl Up Stretch
instructions: Lie on your back with your legs extended and your arms at your sides.
Bend your right knee and bring it towards your chest until thigh is vertical to the floor, interlacing your fingers behind your thigh.
Slowly straighten your right leg, extending your heel towards the ceiling and feeling the stretch in your hamstring. Keep your left leg extended and flat on the floor.
Hold the stretch for 15-30 seconds, then slowly bend your right knee and lower your leg back to the starting position. Repeat on the left side.
tips: Keep your lower back pressed into the floor to maintain proper alignment and support.
Engage your core to stabilize your body and prevent your back from arching.
Move slowly and with control to maximize the stretch and avoid any sudden movements.
results.description: Hamstring Lying Curl Up Stretch is a beginner single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the hamstrings (upper legs). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the flexibility category. Secondary muscles: Calves.

results.name: Hamstring Lying Straight Leg Stretch
instructions: Lie on your back with your legs extended and your arms at your sides.
Lift your right leg towards the ceiling, keeping it straight. Use both hands to gently hold the back of your right leg, just below the knee or higher if possible.
Pull your right leg gently towards your torso, feeling the stretch in your hamstring. Keep your left leg extended and flat on the floor.
Hold the stretch for 15-30 seconds, then slowly lower your right leg back to the starting position. Repeat on the left side.
tips: Move slowly and with control to maximize the stretch and avoid any sudden movements.
Perform the stretch on a comfortable surface, such as a yoga mat, to prevent discomfort or injury.
Only stretch as far as is comfortable without causing pain or discomfort.
results.description: Hamstring Lying Straight Leg Stretch is a beginner single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the hamstrings (upper legs). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the flexibility category. Secondary muscles: Calves.

results.name: Hands Clapped Forearms Stretch
instructions: Stand upright with your feet shoulder width apart and press your palms together in front of your chest with your fingers pointing upward.
Keep your palms together and your elbows lifted as you rotate your hands until your fingers point downward.
Gently lower your joined hands toward your abdomen until you feel a stretch through your wrists and forearms.
Reverse the movement, return your fingers upward, then lower your arms to the starting position.
tips: Rotate your hands slowly without separating them.
Lower your hands only as far as your wrists remain comfortable.
Stop if you feel pain, tingling, or numbness.
Inhale as your fingers point upward and exhale as you lower your hands.
results.description: Hands Clapped Forearms Stretch is an advanced single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the forearms (lower arms). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the flexibility category. Secondary muscles: Biceps, Shoulders.

results.name: Intermediate Hip Flexor and Quad Stretch
instructions: Lie on your stomach with your legs extended and your arms at your sides. Position an elastic cable around your right ankle.
Bend your right knee to bring your foot towards your glutes, holding the elastic cable in your both hands.
Gently pull on the cable to bring your foot closer to your glutes, feeling the stretch in your quadriceps. Hold this position for a moment.

Extend your right leg lightly backwards, allowing the cable to provide resistance and deepen the stretch in your hip flexor and quadriceps. Repeat the movement for the desired number of repetitions, then switch to the left leg.
tips: Focus on deep, steady breathing, inhaling as you extend your leg and exhaling as you pull your foot towards your glutes.
If you find it difficult to reach the cable, use a longer strap or adjust the tension to ensure a comfortable stretch.
Ensure your head and neck remain in a neutral position, looking down towards the floor to avoid strain.
Perform the stretch on a comfortable surface, such as a yoga mat, to prevent discomfort or injury.
results.description: Intermediate Hip Flexor and Quad Stretch is a beginner single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the quads (upper legs). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the flexibility category. Secondary muscles: Glutes.

results.name: Iron Cross Stretch
instructions: Lie on your back with your arms extended out to your sides, forming a T-shape, and your legs extended straight.
Lift your right leg towards the ceiling, keeping it straight, and then lower it across your body towards your left hand while keeping your shoulders flat on the floor.
Allow your right leg to lower as far as comfortably possible, feeling a stretch in your lower back, glutes, and hamstrings.
Hold the stretch for 15-30 seconds, then slowly return your right leg to the starting position. Repeat on the other side with your left leg.
tips: Only stretch as far as is comfortable without causing pain or discomfort.
Perform the stretch on a comfortable surface, such as a yoga mat, to prevent discomfort or injury.
If you have limited flexibility, bend your knee slightly to reduce strain and gradually work towards straightening your leg.
results.description: Iron Cross Stretch is a beginner single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the spine (back). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the flexibility category. Secondary muscles: Hip Flexors.

results.name: Knee to Chest Stretch
instructions: Stand upright with your feet hip-width apart and your arms at your sides.
Lift your right knee towards your chest, wrapping your hands around your knee to gently pull your knee closer to your chest.
Hold the stretch for 15-30 seconds, feeling the stretch. Keep your left leg straight and maintain your balance.
Release your right knee and lower your leg back to the starting position. Repeat the stretch with your left knee. Alternate sides for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Use a gentle but firm grip to avoid pulling too hard and causing strain.
Engage your core to maintain balance and stability throughout the stretch.
Move slowly and with control to maximize the effectiveness of the stretch and avoid any sudden movements.
results.description: Knee to Chest Stretch is a beginner single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the spine (back). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the flexibility category. Secondary muscles: Hip Flexors.

results.name: Kneeling Forearm Flexor Stretch
instructions: Kneel on the floor and place your palms on the floor with your fingers pointing back toward your knees.
Keep your arms straight.
Gently sit back until you feel a stretch along the inside of your forearms.
Hold, breathing steadily, then release.
tips: Go gently; wrists are sensitive.
Keep your palms flat.
results.description: Kneeling Forearm Flexor Stretch is a beginner single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the forearms (lower arms). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the flexibility category.

results.name: Kneeling Hip Flexor Stretch
instructions: Begin in a kneeling position with your right knee on the floor and your left foot in front of you, forming a 90-degree angle with your left knee.
Place your hands on your hips or on your left thigh for support. Engage your core and keep your back straight.
Gently push your hips forward, feeling the stretch in your right hip flexor. Hold the stretch for 15-30 seconds.
Return to the starting position and switch legs, performing the stretch with your left knee on the floor and your right foot in front. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Ensure your front knee is directly above your ankle to avoid putting unnecessary strain on your knee joint.
Maintain an upright posture with your shoulders relaxed and your chest open.
Move slowly and with control to maximize the effectiveness of the stretch and avoid any sudden movements.
results.description: Kneeling Hip Flexor Stretch is a beginner single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the quads (upper legs). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the flexibility category. Secondary muscles: Quadriceps.

results.name: Kneeling Lat Floor Stretch
instructions: Begin in a tabletop position on the floor with your hands directly under your shoulders and your knees under your hips.
Extend your right arm forward on the floor, palm facing up, while keeping your left hand in place.
Bend your left elbow to lower your chest towards the floor, feeling the stretch in your lat muscles and upper back. Keep your head relaxed and look down at the floor.
Hold the stretch for 15-30 seconds, breathing deeply and steadily. Slowly return to the starting position and repeat on the other side by extending your left arm forward and bending your right elbow.
tips: Ensure your extended arm is fully extended to get the most effective stretch in your lats and upper back.
Perform the stretch on a comfortable surface, such as a yoga mat, to prevent discomfort or injury.
Relax your shoulders and neck to avoid tension in these areas.
results.description: Kneeling Lat Floor Stretch is a beginner single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the lats (back). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the flexibility category. Secondary muscles: Upper Back.
